biography.plain_text: Viggo Hieronimus Jarl, born Jørgensen, was a Danish sculptor whose naturalist figures and portraits gained particular recognition in France. Trained in Rome and Paris, he exhibited internationally and co-founded De Frie Billedhuggere. His public works include Marathonløberen and Copenhagen monuments; his estate later funded student housing and grants for sculptors.

long_biography.plain_text:
In 1901, Viggo Hieronimus Jørgensen adopted the surname Jarl and began continental training that would shape his career. He studied in Rome, then at the École des Beaux-Arts and Académie de la Grande Chaumière in Paris. Rodin and the classical tradition informed a naturalist language centred on the human figure, often with psychological or symbolic overtones. He later co-founded De Frie Billedhuggere and helped secure a dedicated sculpture hall for the group.

Jarl divided his working life between Denmark and France, eventually settling in Cannes. His sculptures ranged from portraits and solitary figures to Marathonløberen and monumental commissions for Copenhagen's Marble Church. Exhibitions across Europe and the United States gave the work an international audience. Born into an industrial family, he inherited substantial holdings that enabled an unusually independent artistic life. His will redirected much of the estate into a foundation, student housing and grants for sculptors.
